The Brooklyn Nets are an American professional basketball team.
The Brooklyn Nets are based in the New York City borough of Brooklyn.
The Brooklyn Nets compete in the National Basketball Association (NBA).
The Brooklyn Nets play their home games at Barclays Center.
The Brooklyn Nets are one of two NBA teams located in New York City.
The other NBA team in New York City is the New York Knicks.
The Brooklyn Nets were established in 1967 as a charter franchise of the NBA's rival league, the American Basketball Association (ABA).
The Brooklyn Nets initially played in Teaneck, New Jersey, as the New Jersey Americans.
In its early years, the team led a nomadic existence, moving to Long Island and playing there as the New York Nets.
Led by Hall of Famer Julius "Dr. J" Erving, the Nets won two ABA championships before becoming one of four ABA teams admitted into the NBA in 1976.

Unlike the other three ABA teams entering the NBA, who played in cities without any NBA presence, the Nets were required to pay an "encroachment fee" of $4.8 million (equivalent to $26 million in 2023) to the New York Knicks.
The team financed that payment by selling Erving's contract to the Philadelphia 76ers.
The Nets went from winning the last ABA title in 1975–76 to having the worst record in the NBA in 1976–77.
In 1977, the team returned to New Jersey and played as the New Jersey Nets from 1977 to 2012.
Led by star point guard Jason Kidd, the Nets reached the NBA Finals in two consecutive NBA seasons (2001–02 and 2002–03).
In the summer of 2012, the team moved to Barclays Center in Brooklyn.
The move from New Jersey to Brooklyn was approved unanimously by the NBA Board of Governors on April 13, 2012.
The Brooklyn Nets have qualified for the playoffs on eight occasions since moving to Brooklyn.
The Brooklyn Nets reached the Conference Semifinals in 2014 and 2021.
During the early 2000s, the Nets were led by Jason Kidd and Kenyon Martin, while the Boston Celtics were experiencing newfound success behind Paul Pierce and Antoine Walker.
The rivalry between the Nets and Celtics began to heat up in the 2002 Eastern Conference Finals.
Celtic fans berated Kidd and his family with chants of "Wife Beater!" in response to Kidd's 2001 domestic abuse charge.
Nets fans responded by brandishing signs that read "Will someone please stab Paul Pierce?" referring to a night club incident in 2000 where Pierce was stabbed 11 times.
Bill Walton said at the time that Nets-Celtics was the "beginning of the next great NBA rivalry" during the Eastern Conference Finals in 2002.
Led by Kidd, the Nets advanced to the NBA Finals in 2002 and swept Boston in the 2003 playoffs.
On November 28, 2012, an altercation occurred on the court between Rajon Rondo, Gerald Wallace, and Kris Humphries, resulting in their ejection.
Rajon Rondo was suspended for two games following the altercation.
Gerald Wallace and Kevin Garnett were fined after the altercation.
Kyrie Irving signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2019.
Kyrie Irving's signing caused many Celtics fans to blame him for the Celtics' inability to get through to the playoffs.
During a regular season game between the Celtics and Nets in the 2019–20 season, Celtics fans chanted "Kyrie sucks" at TD Garden.
When the series returned to Brooklyn two days later, Nets fans chanted "Kyrie's better" in response to the chants in Boston.
On May 30, 2021, Kyrie Irving stomped on the Celtics logo center court after a Nets victory and a 3–1 lead in the series.
A fan threw a water bottle at Kyrie Irving at TD Garden following the Nets' victory.

The Brooklyn Nets' former primary logo, used from 2012 until 2017, featured "Brooklyn" in front of both the white and black uniforms.

The Brooklyn Nets wore three different alternate uniforms: a grey-sleeved alternate with "Brooklyn" in Dodger blue (first used in 2013), a white-sleeved alternate with the team name in black (featured the same "Stars and Stripes" look from the 1970s), and a dark grey sleeveless alternate that recalled the 1980s New Jersey Nets uniforms.
The Brooklyn Nets' current primary logo, used since 2017, features "Brooklyn" in front of both the white and black uniforms.

The Brooklyn Nets have had three different versions of the "Statement" uniform: a dark grey base with "BKLYN" in white (first set), a lighter grey base with black/dark grey stripes and "BKLYN" written in graffiti style designed by Eric Haze, and a black base with black letters with silver trim and a subtle greyscale herringbone striping with three black stars on the left.
The Brooklyn Nets' "City" uniform for 2017–18 featured the full team name spelled in white along with grey accents inspired from the Brooklyn Bridge.
For the following season, the Brooklyn Nets replaced the "City" uniform with a black uniform featuring stylized Brooklyn camo patterns as a tribute to The Notorious B.I.G.

In 2019–20, the Brooklyn Nets wore white versions of the "Biggie" uniforms with Haze-designed "BED-STUY" graffiti lettering in front (a reference to Bedford–Stuyvesant where The Notorious B.I.G. grew up).
The 2020–21 "City" uniform honored Brooklyn-born artist Jean-Michel Basquiat and was predominantly black with "BKLYN NETS" written in Basquiat's style along with multi-colored striping.

The 2022–23 "City" uniform featured visual references to the Nets' uniform history, including a navy base and white and silver argyle stripes recalling the 1997–2009 uniforms, the "Nets" wordmark and lettering from the 1990–97 uniforms, a red stripe with white stars honoring the "Stars and Stripes" uniform of the 1970s and 1980s, and a modified version of the 1980s New Jersey Nets logo.

The Brooklyn Nets' "Earned" uniform is released occasionally and is exclusive only to teams that qualified in the NBA playoffs the previous year. The Nets were given an "Earned" uniform by virtue of qualifying in the 2020 NBA playoffs, featuring the herringbone parquet style of the Barclays Center court in shades of black and grey with Helvetica lettering inspired from signs found at the New York City Subway.
The mascot of the New Jersey Nets was Sly the Silver Fox, who debuted on October 31, 1997.
Prior to that, the Nets' mascot was an anthropomorphic dragon named Duncan the Dragon.
After the Nets moved to Brooklyn in 2012, they introduced a new superhero mascot named BrooklyKnight (a pun on the demonym "Brooklynite") on November 3, 2012.
The Brooklyn Brigade is a group of fans known for their loud chants and passionate attitude towards the Nets.
The Brooklyn Brigade was founded in November 2012 by Udong "Bobby" Edemeka.
Mr. Whammy, an iconic 86-year-old Nets superfan, became a season ticket holder in 1998 when the Nets played in Continental Airlines Arena.
Joseph Tsai, executive vice chairman of Alibaba Group, completed the acquisition of full ownership of the Brooklyn Nets on September 18, 2019.
With the closing of the transaction, Tsai became NBA Governor of the Nets and its affiliates.
David Levy was named CEO of the Nets and Barclays Center in November 12, 2019.
Oliver Weisberg assumed an interim CEO role after David Levy stepped down from his position on November 12, 2019.
The original owner of the Nets franchise was trucking magnate Arthur J. Brown, who founded the team in 1967.
In 1968, Brown sold the team for $1.1 million to entrepreneur Roy Boe.

Due to financial losses suffered while the team was on Long Island, Boe moved the team back to New Jersey in 1977 and sold it a year later to a group of seven local businessmen led by Alan N. Cohen and Joseph Taub, known as the "Secaucus Seven".

The "Secaucus Seven" finally sold the team in 1998 to a group of local real estate developers led by Raymond Chambers and Lewis Katz, who called themselves the "Community Youth Organization" and wanted to move the team to Newark, New Jersey.

In 1999, the Community Youth Organization signed an agreement with New York Yankees owner George Steinbrenner to form YankeeNets, a holding company that owned the two teams and increased leverage in future broadcast contracts by negotiating together.
After receiving offers from several broadcast partners, including Cablevision, YankeeNets decided to launch its own regional sports television called the YES Network.
YankeeNets failed in their attempts to secure a deal with Newark to construct a new arena in the city.
By that point, tensions between the management of the Yankees, Nets, and Devils had caused a rift between them, leading to the group's split.
The "Secaucus Seven" placed the team up for sale after their plan to move the Nets dead.
In 2004, real estate developer Bruce Ratner purchased the team with the intent of moving it to a new arena in Brooklyn as part of the large-scale Atlantic Yards development.
Rapper Jay-Z owned a small minority stake in the Nets from 2003 until 2013.
Jay-Z helped encourage the move from New Jersey to the Barclays Center in Brooklyn and held a stake in the arena.
On September 24, 2009, Mikhail Prokhorov confirmed his intention to become majority owner of the Nets.
Prokhorov funded a loan of $700 million for the construction of Barclays Center and attracted additional funds from Western banks.
On May 11, 2010, following approval from other NBA teams' owners, Prokhorov became the principal owner of the Nets.
In late 2017, Prokhorov agreed to sell a 49% stake in the team to Joseph Tsai with an option for Tsai to become the majority owner.
The option was exercised in August 2019, and Tsai also bought the Nets' arena, Barclays Center, from Prokhorov for nearly $1 billion in a separate deal.
The NBA Board of Governors unanimously approved the sale to Tsai on September 18, 2019.
The Nets' practice facility is located at the Hospital for Special Surgery Training Center in Industry City complex in Sunset Park neighborhood of Brooklyn.
The facility opened on February 17, 2016, and occupies 70,000 square feet of space.
Prior to that, the team practiced at PNY Center in East Rutherford, New Jersey (opened in 1998), APA Recreation Center in North Bergen, New Jersey, and Ramapo College in Mahwah, New Jersey.

In the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy in November 2012, PNY Center suffered a power outage and extensive water damage, leading to the team using smaller training spaces inside Barclays Center for several months.
